8.4 Dispute Resolution and Audit Rights. For invoice disputes, Publisher shall notify Licensor within seven (7) days. The Parties will work in good faith to resolve. Publisher shall pay undisputed amounts per schedule. Licensor may not suspend the Licensed Digital Format due to unpaid amounts subject to a good faith dispute. In the event of any identified overpayment, Publisher may offset such amounts against future royalties or require Licensor to refund the overpayment within thirty (30) days of written notice. During the Term, Licensor shall have the right, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice and no more than once per calendar year, to engage an independent third-party auditor to audit Publisher's Gamestart records at Licensor's expense, provided that any such audit: (a) shall be conducted during Publisher's regular business hours, (b) all information collected shall be treated as Confidential Information of Publisher, (c) access to records is restricted to verifying the accuracy of Gamestart calculations and royalty payments under this Section 8, and (d) Publisher has thirty (30) days to cure any discrepancy identified. Any such audit is subject to Publisher's reasonable security protocols. Publisher shall maintain complete and accurate Gamestart records for not less than two (2) years following the end of the Term.

Section 2.  Restricted Activities.  Tenant shall not, without Landlord’s prior written consent, which
: (a) provide overnight inpatient care or overnight boarding of patients at the Leased Premises; (b) store, use, or dispose of Hazardous Materials
(including regulated medical waste, sharps, pathological and pharmaceutical waste, hazardous drugs, radiologic and nuclear materials, fixatives, sterilant gases, and controlled substances)

at the Leased Premises other than in types and quantities customary for, and in compliance with applicable law governing, outpatient medical and diagnostic practices of the kind Tenant operates, including routine clinical, laboratory, and pharmaceutical materials;

(c) conduct any activity that would void or materially increase the cost of Landlord’s building insurance, provided Landlord shall first notify Tenant of any such increased cost and afford Tenant a reasonable opportunity to cease the activity giving rise to it before treating the same as a default.

Without limiting the foregoing, twenty-four-hour, walk-in, or emergency operations require Landlord’s separate prior written consent, a written security plan, dedicated after-hours access control, and corresponding insurance and indemnity satisfactory to Landlord. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Tenant shall not add any service involving controlled substances, radiologic or nuclear materials, hazardous-drug compounding, laboratory testing above CLIA-waived complexity, or a material increase in regulated medical-waste volume without at least thirty (30) days’ prior written notice, delivery of applicable licenses and updated insurance certificates, and Landlord’s prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld. Tenant shall pay all additional costs attributable to its operations, including after-hours HVAC, utilities, security, supplemental janitorial, and overflow parking.
